newsitem.title: USA: Congress clears bill to lift U.S. tuna embargo.
newsitem.headline: Congress clears bill to lift U.S. tuna embargo.

text.p: The House of Representatives Thursday approved a compromise version of a bill to lift the U.S. embargo on tuna caught in nets that also may snare dolphins and sent the legislation to President Clinton.
The House unanimously agreed to changes the Senate made in the legislation to move it to the White House before the Congress starts its month-long recess.

The legislation, sought by the White House at the urging of Mexico, would lift the embargo once an international agreement among Mexico, Venezuela and other nations is in effect to use measures that protect dolphins.

The United States imposed the embargo in 1994 after a public outcry over the slaughter of hundreds of thousands of dolphins that were drowned and slashed by the huge encircling nets used to catch tuna in the Eastern Tropical Pacific Ocean.
To regain entry into the U.S. market, those countries have adopted measures to free dolphin caught in the nets and minimise deaths.

But to ensure that dolphin are not harmed, the bill would not allow cans of tuna caught in the encircling nets to be labeled as "dolphin safe" until March 1999 after a study on dolphin populations is done.
